description: The European Investment Bank (EIB) project record for the Seine-Nord Europe Canal describes the construction of a new 107 km class Vb inland waterway between Compiègne and Aubencheul-au-Bac in France, promoted by the Société du Canal Seine-Nord Europe. The canal is the central link of the cross-border Seine-Scheldt project, an EU priority project since 2004 and a pre-identified project on the North Sea - Mediterranean core network corridor of the Trans-European Transport Network, connecting the Seine and Scheldt basins and several inland ports. Coverage: project purpose (larger vessels, lower operating costs, lower environmental costs than road), an EIB loan of EUR 800 million signed on 20 December 2022, a total cost of about EUR 6,651 million, and a public register of the French environmental and social impact assessment volumes from November 2022, covering the technical description, alternatives, water and aquatic environments, protected species derogations, land clearing, effects on existing canals, construction-phase effects and health. Format and access: an HTML page linking PDF documents, mostly in French. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated. Caveats: costs and dates are those recorded by the EIB and may change as works proceed. The planned link can be added as a future edge in freight network flow and capacity planning models of northern Europe. It relates to ES-TRIN and the Congo basin inland navigation data in the catalogue.
